title: Bin night
summary: Somebody has been through your bins, and on Sunday there's a story about what you eat. You know who. A season on, he wants a favour.

ends.title: The favour
ends.text: A reporter went through your bins. A season later you let him have the story he wanted, and he owes you.

ends.title: Locked bins
ends.text: Your bins have a lock on them now. The reporter still writes about you, from further away.

beats.title: Sunday

event.title: Sunday
event.speaker: tabloid
setup: Sunday's {tabloid.outlet}: "STAR'S SECRET TAKEAWAY SHAME", with a photo of a pizza box and four kebab wrappers on your drive. {tabloid.name}'s name is on it. The pizza box was your brother's.

say: He rings you himself on Monday, cheerful. "No hard feelings. Want to give me a quote? Say it was a cheat day. Everyone loves a cheat day."

quote.text: "STAR: IT WAS MY CHEAT DAY." It goes down well. A pizza place offers you a deal.

brother.text: "STAR BLAMES BROTHER." Your brother rings you, and then the paper, and makes it worse.

angry.text: You buy a bin with a padlock. It's in the paper the next Sunday: "STAR LOCKS BINS."

beats.hint: There's a story about your bins

beats.title: The favour

event.title: The favour
event.speaker: tabloid
setup: A season on. {tabloid.short} rings. His editor wants a picture of you at home, a real one, for a feature, and he's got a week.
{if arc.path=='locked'}"I won't touch the bins. Promise."{/if}

choices.label: "Come round Thursday. Bring your own milk."

outcomes.text: He comes round, drinks his own milk and gets a nice photo of you and the dog next door. He sends a bottle at Christmas with a card: "Owe you."
He does the feature anyway, with a photo of your front door from across the road.

beats.hint: A season on, the reporter wants something
